note:
762 -> 761 (-1). Measured as CI does: ruff check odoo/ with the committed toolchain, scope odoo/ only.

The unit is odoo/libs/__init__.py, rewritten from an eager re-export block to a PEP 562 lazy facade. The old form was one long chain of 'from .X import (a, b, c, ...)' statements; the new one resolves through a module __getattr__ over a name->area table, which retires the lint the eager block carried.

The change is not a lint fix -- that is a side effect. odoo.libs is the dependency-free layer and is imported almost everywhere, and its eager '.text' re-export pulled libs/text/html.py, i.e. lxml + lxml.html.clean + markupsafe + arabic_reshaper, into every consumer that touched any libs symbol. Measured in a fresh interpreter: 'from odoo.libs.collections import Collector' (a ~30-line helper) loaded 137 modules including lxml and markupsafe before, and 75 with no heavy third party after (this interpreter's own baseline is 63, so the odoo cost falls from 74 modules to 12). Re-measure with: python -c 'import sys; from odoo.libs.collections import Collector; print(len(sys.modules))'. Pinned by odoo/libs/tests/test_facade_is_lazy.py, which runs the measurement in a subprocess (sys.modules cannot answer it in-session) and carries a control asserting odoo.libs.text still IS the heavy area, so the other assertions cannot pass vacuously.

Note what this did NOT fix, since the docstring originally overclaimed it: importing odoo.orm.components.model_graph still loads babel, because orm/__init__.py's last line is 'import odoo.init' (the bootstrap, which applies _monkeypatches). Traced, not assumed. libs was a second, independent path to the same stack, not the only one.
